message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules**

| Section | What you need to know |
|---------|-----------------------|
| **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever house rule you set). Points are earned by being the first to empty your hand in each round. |
| **Players** | 2–10 (standard deck works best with 4–8). |
| **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue) × 25 cards each (one 0, two 1–9, two “Draw Two”, two “Skip”, two “Reverse”), plus 4 “Wild” and 4 “Wild Draw Four”. |
| **Setup** | 1. Shuffle the deck. 2. Deal 7 cards to each player. 3. Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile. 4. Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. If it’s a special card, apply its effect immediately (e.g., if it’s a “Draw Two”, the first player draws two cards and loses a turn). |

---

### How to Play

| Turn | What to do |
|------|------------|
| **1. Match** | On your turn, play one card that matches the **color**, **number**, or **symbol** of the top discard. |
| **2. Wild** | You may play a “Wild” or “Wild Draw Four” on any card. When you play a wild, you must declare the new color. |
| **3. Draw** | If you cannot play a card, draw one from the draw pile. If that card can be played, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. |
| **4. End of Turn** | If you played a card that ends the round (i.e., you have no cards left), shout “UNO!” when you have one card left. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two cards as a penalty. |

---

### Special Cards

| Card | Effect |
|------|--------|
| **Draw Two** | Next player draws two cards and skips their turn. |
| **Skip** | Next player loses their turn. |
| **Reverse** | Reverses the direction of play (clockwise ↔ counter‑clockwise). With two players, it acts like a Skip. |
| **Wild** | Player chooses the next color. |
| **Wild Draw Four** | Player chooses the next color; next player draws four cards and skips their turn. **Can only be played if you have no matching color cards.** If challenged and you were allowed to play it, the challenger draws four cards instead. |

---

### Scoring

| Round | How points are tallied |
|-------|------------------------|
| **Winner** | Adds up the values of all cards remaining in opponents’ hands: |
| | • Number cards = face value. |
| | • Draw Two, Skip, Reverse = 20 points each. |
| | • Wild, Wild Draw Four = 50 points each. |
| **Next round** | Continue until someone reaches the target score (usually 500). |

---

### Common Variations (House Rules)

| Variation | What changes |
|-----------|--------------|
| **No “Wild Draw Four” challenge** | Players can’t challenge; the card is always legal. |
| **“Stacking”** | If a player plays a Draw Two or Wild Draw Four, the next player can stack another of the same type instead of drawing. |
| **“Uno” penalty** | If you forget to say “UNO” before your next turn, you must draw two cards. |
| **“Skip” on “Wild”** | Some groups allow a “Skip” to be played on a Wild. |
| **“Draw to 21”** | Instead of 500 points, play until someone reaches 21 points. |

---

### Quick Tips

1. **Keep a mix of colors** – Having cards of many colors reduces the chance you’ll be stuck.
2. **Save your Wilds** – Use them strategically to change the color when you’re low on cards.
3. **Watch opponents** – If someone is close to “UNO”, be ready to call them out if they forget.
4. **Plan for “Reverse”** – In a 2‑player game, a Reverse is a Skip; use it to skip an opponent’s turn.

That’s the core of Uno! Once you’ve played a few rounds, the flow will feel natural, and you can start experimenting with house rules to keep things fresh. Enjoy the colorful chaos!
